q: A diagram which shows the variation of axial force is called
explanation: A thrust diagram plots the variation of axial (normal) force along a member.

q: A beam of uniform strength will have at every cross-section the same
explanation: A beam of uniform strength is designed so bending stress remains constant at every section, by varying the section dimensions.

q: If a beam is loaded transversely, the maximum compressive stress develops on
explanation: For typical sagging (downward transverse load), the top fiber is in maximum compression.

q: In a beam, the neutral plane
options: passes through the c.g. of the area of c/s
explanation: As per the answer key for this set (note: the standard textbook fact is that the neutral axis passes through the centroid of the cross-section — worth double-checking against your source book).

q: Longitudinal cracks observed in timber beams are due to
options: application of concentrated loads over the beam
explanation: As per the answer key for this set (note: longitudinal splitting along the grain in timber is classically attributed to horizontal shear failure between layers — worth double-checking against your source book).

q: The expression EI d⁴y/dx⁴ at any section for a beam is equal to
explanation: Differentiating the beam equation twice more: EI·d⁴y/dx⁴ = w, the load intensity.

q: The slope of curve of B.M. diagram at any section will be equal to
options: the slope of loading at that section
the slope of shear force diagram at that section
the ordinate of shear force diagram at that section
the area of shear force diagram starting from any one end
explanation: Since dM/dx = V, the slope of the BM curve at any point equals the SF value (ordinate) there.

q: The slope of curve of S.F. diagram at any section will be equal to
options: the slope of loading at that section
the ordinate of loading diagram at that section
the area of loading diagram from end to that section
the bending moment at that section
explanation: Since dV/dx = -w, the slope of the SF curve equals the load intensity ordinate at that section.

q: The difference between BM values at any two sections will be equal to
options: the area of SF diagram between those two sections
the area of loading diagram between the two sections
the area of bending moment between the two sections
explanation: ΔM between two sections equals the area under the shear force diagram between them (∫V dx).

q: The difference between SF values at any two sections will be equal to
options: the area of bending moment between the two sections
the difference between the slopes of the curve of loading diagram at two sections
the ordinate of shear force diagram at one section plus the slope of the loading diagram multiplied by the distance between two sections
the area of the loading diagram between those two sections
explanation: ΔV between two sections equals the area under the load intensity diagram between them (∫w dx).

q: The bending moment in a cable carrying a system of loads will be
explanation: A flexible cable carries load purely by axial tension along its curved shape — it develops no bending moment anywhere.

q: A member with a cross section of a mm² is subjected to a force of P N. It is L mm long and of Young's Modulus, E N/mm². The strain will be
explanation: Strain = stress/E = (P/A)/E = P/AE, a dimensionless ratio (mm/mm).

q: Find the elongation of a bar if c/s area of bar is A, length l, applied load p, modulus of elasticity of material is E
explanation: Standard elongation formula: δ = PL/AE.

q: If α is the coefficient of linear expansion, T is the rise in temperature then thermal stress is given by
explanation: Thermal stress (fully restrained) = E·α·T.

q: Thrust is induced in case of
explanation: Thrust (axial force along the member) develops from the component of an inclined load along the member's axis.

q: The diagram showing the variation of axial load along the span is called
explanation: Axial load variation along a member's length is plotted as a thrust diagram.

q: The number of points of contraflexure in a simply supported beam carrying UDL, is
explanation: A simply supported beam under UDL sags throughout its span, so BM never changes sign — zero contraflexure points.

q: BM in a cantilever beam having span 1.8m and uniformly distributed load of 4kg/m
A point where SF is zero, BM is
explanation: Where SF=0, BM reaches a local extremum — this could be either a maximum (sagging peak) or minimum (hogging peak) depending on the loading.

q: The rate of change of shear force is called
explanation: dV/dx = -w — the rate of change of shear force equals the load intensity.

q: Which of the following sections is the most efficient in carrying bending moments?
explanation: I-sections concentrate material in the flanges, far from the neutral axis, giving the best moment-carrying efficiency per unit area.

q: Find the value of thrust, if the member (beam) is subjected to an inclined force having magnitude 5 kN and inclination with vertical is 30°
explanation: Thrust (component along the horizontal beam axis) = 5 × sin30° = 2.5 kN.

q: At the point of application of a concentrated load on a beam, there is
options: sudden change of slope of BM
explanation: A point load causes a sudden jump (discontinuity) in the shear force diagram, which produces a sudden change in the slope of the BM diagram at that point.
